body.statement: On any two-policy face where schedule types are constant within each retained slice, the support linear program furnished by Theorem 1 reduces to the bivariate coupling program for the two slice-level potential welfares; its extremal covariance bounds are the comonotone and countermonotone Fréchet--Hoeffding bounds used by AronowGreenLee2014.
body.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against the established two-potential-outcome sharp bound.
body.gap: The reduction is known in the two-margin setting; its role here is validation rather than a standalone novelty claim.
body.consumer: Implementations can test the multi-slice LP against a closed-form two-policy benchmark before analyzing the three-policy menu.
